solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Belittled a duke touring HQ

indicators.note: touring means going all round, so the first pair of letters encloses the headquarters word

parts.note: a headquarters is a base

explanation.surface: A nobleman visiting headquarters is made to feel small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts A and D around BASE, the A at the front and the D at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase someone is to humble or degrade them, so abased is a synonym of belittled.

clue.text: Sportsman in short shorts

indicators.note: short tells us the word that follows is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: boxers are a kind of men's shorts

explanation.surface: An athlete wearing very brief shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last S from BOXERS, a type of shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is an athlete who fights in the ring, an example of a sportsman.

clue.text: Most rigorous examination following poor crits

indicators.note: following places the examination word after the shuffled letters
poor suggests the critiques are badly put together, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: an examination is a test

explanation.surface: The toughest exam comes after some bad critiques.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' signals the anagram of the critiques, and 'following' puts the exam word last.
explanation.definitionFit: Strictest is the superlative of strict, meaning the most severe or exacting, matching most rigorous.

clue.text: Willing to learn from medical man, the Italian head of embryology

parts.note: a doctor is informally a doc
il is the Italian for the

indicators.note: head of means take just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An eager student of a doctor who leads an Italian embryology department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' takes E from embryology.
explanation.definitionFit: Docile originally meant teachable, from Latin docere to teach, so it fits a pupil keen to learn.

clue.text: Don, perhaps, has fed FBI agent

indicators.note: fed means put inside, as food goes into a mouth, so the verb for possessing goes into the agent

parts.note: a G-man is American slang for an FBI agent
to have something is to own it, so has gives owns

explanation.surface: A university lecturer has given information to the FBI.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed' signals insertion and also hints at a Fed, an American federal agent; 'Don' looks like a man's name but is a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A gownsman is a member of a university who wears an academic gown, and a don is one example.

clue.text: Concede one must have let the cat out of the bag?

definitions.meaning: to concede is to hand the match over to the opponent, literally surrendering it

definitions.text: let the cat out of the bag?
definitions.meaning: to let the cat out of the bag is to reveal a secret by accident

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both surrendering a contest literally and revealing a secret, matching each definition in turn.

clue.text: Tie up tie over in officers' mess

indicators.note: over in a down clue signals the whole run of letters is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to tie up a boat is to moor it
a tied game is a draw

explanation.surface: Fastening a necktie over again in the officers' dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns MOORDRAW into WARDROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The wardroom is the room on a warship where commissioned officers eat, their mess.

clue.text: Hebridean island without a workforce

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter named is dropped from the island

parts.note: Staffa is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off Scotland, famous for Fingal's Cave

explanation.surface: A Scottish island with no labour force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the final A from STAFFA, an uninhabited island off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The staff of an organisation are its employees, the people who make up its workforce.

clue.text: Notice over embassy entrance

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: an advertisement is a notice, abbreviated to ad
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: A sign hung above the doorway of a foreign embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission means being let in, an entrance into a place, as in admission to a club.

clue.text: Additional clothing fielder required

parts.note: additional means extra
a cover is something worn over the body

explanation.surface: Someone asks for more layers of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Extra cover is a cricket fielding position on the off side, between cover point and mid-off.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the fielder stationed at extra cover is known by the name of that position.

clue.text: Member meeting unknown host

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns, here Y

explanation.surface: A club member is introduced to a mysterious party host.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large crowd or multitude, especially a fighting force, so army is a synonym.

clue.text: Couple hired band

parts.note: a brace is a pair, a couple
let means rented out, hired

explanation.surface: A pair of people engaged a music group.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a decorative band worn around the wrist.

clue.text: Say no to litter

definitions.meaning: to turn down or decline an offer

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means decline and the noun, stressed differently, means rubbish, matching each definition.

clue.text: One makes notes in 'Oxford Book of Essays', initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each word of the book title

explanation.surface: Someone takes notes on a collection of Oxford essays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of Oxford Book of Essays.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a woodwind instrument, a thing that makes musical notes.

clue.text: Nash, say — name in fashion with high society

parts.note: Beau Nash was an 18th-century dandy who ruled fashionable society in Bath, an example of a beau

indicators.note: in places the name abbreviation inside the word for fashion

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style

explanation.surface: A Regency dandy famous in fashion mingles with the upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside MODE to give MONDE. A beau is a dandy, and Beau Nash was the famous one at Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau monde is French for fine world, the fashionable elite, so it means high society.

clue.text: Former wife's erotic dancing is popular

parts.note: an ex is a former wife or partner

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ex-wife's racy dance moves are a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges EROTIC into OTERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Exoteric means suitable for or understood by the general public, so popular rather than for an inner circle.

clue.text: Clear as to changes in a financial clause

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the preceding phrase are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to clarify alterations in a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the nine letters of CLEAR AS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalator clause in a contract lets prices or wages rise in line with costs, a financial provision.

clue.text: Repent, possibly, before church reveals sham

indicators.note: before places the shuffled letters ahead of the church abbreviation
possibly means the word could be arranged another way, so its letters are shuffled

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Showing remorse just before going to church exposes a hypocrite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram, and 'before' sets the shuffled letters ahead of the Church of England abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a false show or act, so it is a synonym of sham.

clue.text: Crab tea, I suspect, could be the cause of food poisoning

indicators.note: suspect describes something dubious, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A diner fears crab and tea have made them ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' looks like the speaker's guess, but 'suspect' is the anagram signal and 'I' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria such as salmonella are microbes responsible for many cases of food poisoning.

clue.text: Sugar source for preserve, ultimate in marmalade

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins

indicators.note: ultimate in means take the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Where the sugar for marmalade comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate in' takes E from marmalade.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar cane is a tall grass whose stems are a major source of sugar.

clue.text: A lot of money got from breaking the law

indicators.note: breaking means smashing up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fortune made by committing crimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges THE LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth is an abundance of riches, so it means a lot of money.

clue.text: A stubborn type beginning to trust a lucky charm

parts.note: a mule is proverbially stubborn

indicators.note: beginning to means take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An obstinate person starts to rely on a talisman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes T from trust.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a small object worn to ward off harm, a protective lucky charm.

clue.text: Game, extremely tight once opener's removed

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, and removed means it is taken away

parts.note: blotto is slang for extremely drunk, or tight

explanation.surface: A game that was once very close loses its first player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener's removed' takes B off BLOTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance in which numbers are drawn, like bingo or a lottery.

clue.text: Say about the old girl's monocle

indicators.note: about means going round, so the abbreviation for say encloses the old article

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does
ye is an old form of the
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Talk about the old lady's eyepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the example abbreviation goes round the archaic article; ye is the old spelling of the seen on pub signs.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeglass is a single lens for one eye, which is what a monocle is.

clue.text: Man of high social standing also blowing top

indicators.note: blowing top means losing the top letter, in a down clue the first one

parts.note: as well means also

explanation.surface: A posh gentleman also loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' takes A off AS WELL. 'blowing top' reads as losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is an old informal word for a fashionable person of high rank.

clue.text: Shore bird in difficulty

definitions.meaning: a small wading sandpiper seen on coasts
a tangle or problem, as in tying oneself up

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a wading bird of the sandpiper family and also a tangle or problem.

clue.text: Fresh landlord brought round special bulletin

indicators.note: brought round means the two words are placed around the abbreviation for special

parts.note: fresh means new
a letter is one who lets property, a landlord

explanation.surface: A new landlord delivers a special news sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' signals the container. A letter here is one who lets property, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsletter is a regular printed report of news sent to members, a bulletin.

clue.text: Picking up on insurance policy, at last

parts.note: re means on or concerning
cover is insurance protection

indicators.note: at last means take the final letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Claiming on an insurance policy, at long last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes Y from policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovery is improvement or a revival, as when an economy is said to be picking up.

clue.text: Messenger carried on about artist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for carried on goes round the artist

parts.note: to have held on is to have carried on, kept going
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A courier kept going on about a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald is an official who carries messages and proclamations, a messenger.
